title: One name, one kind of thing
statement: Never reuse a name for a different kind of thing across lessons read in sequence.
detail: A review of a Grade 5 unit found the same names used for a person in one lesson and for a source or record in the next, so that, read in order, the same tokens kept changing what kind of thing they named; it called the fix cheap and the confusion high if left (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19.md`). It rests on that one finding.

evidence.quote: same tokens keep changing referent class. Cheap to fix (rename L6's sources or L4's
"Mood" here means a character's passing feeling, while L4 taught mood as how a place feels.
